package_info.package_versions: all published versions (approx. 4 weeks before takedown)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain multi-phase malicious code that downloads, installs, and runs a cryptocurrency miner on Linux systems, abusing system resources for unauthorized mining and potentially compromising device and network security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code decodes a base64-encoded payload and executes it, which initiates the next stage of the attack by running additional malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code execution at import-time is a common technique to hide malicious payloads and evade static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not execute obfuscated or hidden code automatically upon import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in proprietary code to protect intellectual property, but not in open-source packages without clear justification.

execution_context.file_location: Decoded and executed by snippet_1; likely in a temporary file or in-memory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fetches a remote shell script from a malicious URL and executes it, which retrieves configuration for the coinminer.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote scripts is a classic method for delivering second-stage payloads and is rarely justified in legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download and execute arbitrary code from the internet without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers may fetch dependencies, but not hidden scripts from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: remote URL not associated with legitimate infrastructure

execution_context.trigger: runtime (as part of shell script from snippet_2)
execution_context.file_location: Temporary directory or user home directory (e.g., /tmp/coinminer)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a coinminer binary from a GitLab repository, makes it executable, and runs it in the background to mine cryptocurrency.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a binary from an untrusted remote source is highly suspicious, especially when run in the background.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not install or run background processes unrelated to their stated functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may fetch binaries, but only from trusted sources and with user consent.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (as part of shell script from snippet_2)
execution_context.file_location: Temporary directory or user home directory

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: while true; do pgrep coinminer || /tmp/coinminer; sleep 60; done &
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code ensures the coinminer process is always running by restarting it if it stops, maintaining persistence for the mining operation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Persistence mechanisms that automatically restart unauthorized processes are a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not create persistent background processes without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System daemons may use similar logic, but only for legitimate, user-approved services.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated code execution at import-time (e.g., base64 decoding and exec)
Automatic download and execution of remote shell scripts
Fetching and running binaries from untrusted sources (e.g., GitLab)
Persistence mechanisms that monitor and restart unauthorized processes
file_indicators: Temporary files or binaries in /tmp or user home directory (e.g., /tmp/coinminer)
Presence of shell scripts or configuration files fetched from remote URLs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains (e.g., GitLab repositories not associated with the package author)
Fetching shell scripts or binaries from remote URLs during package installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that execute obfuscated code at import-time, especially those using base64 decoding and exec. Flag any package that downloads and executes remote shell scripts or binaries from untrusted sources. Detect persistence mechanisms that monitor and restart unauthorized processes. Watch for network activity to suspicious domains (e.g., GitLab URLs not linked to the package author) and the creation of unexpected binaries in temporary directories.
